newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call easy on lower demand, gilts inactive.
newsitem.headline: Indian call easy on lower demand, gilts inactive.

text.p: Indian call money opened steady at 2.50-3.50 percent on Tuesday, dealers said.
Call rates were at 1.75-2.25 percent in the latest quotes, they said.

Dealers expect call rates to see some tightness in the next fortnight. "The advance tax outflow and the 20-billion rupee seven year bond auction will suck out the existing liquidity to a major extent," a dealer said.
An ongoing strike at State Bank of India (SBI)'s Bombay office, if continued next week, will also help a rally in call rates, dealers said.
Most dealers expect the cut-off rate of 12.55-12.65 percent at the seven-year bond auction on Tuesday evening.
The securities market was largely inactive as dealers awaited the outcome of the bond auction.
